summary.name: Fitness tracker
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia overview of fitness trackers (activity trackers), electronic wearables that measure movement and physiological data such as steps, heart rate, sleep and calorie expenditure.
use_cases: understand how wearables track heart rate and activity
research wearable use in medicine and stress monitoring
learn about privacy risks of health tracking apps
background reading on quantified self devices
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article describing fitness trackers and their history, from early heart rate monitors and bicycle computers to modern wristbands, rings, earphones and smartwatches. It explains the sensors these devices use (accelerometers, altimeters, heart rate sensors) and the metrics they report, such as steps, distance, heart rate, calories and sleep. It summarizes research on uses in medicine, including atrial fibrillation detection, weight loss, stress monitoring and Parkinson's prediction. It also covers accuracy limits and privacy concerns around data collection and sharing.
notable: Covers wrist, ring and earphone tracker formats and their trade-offs
Summarizes studies on physical activity gains and mixed weight-loss results
Discusses privacy issues with fitness apps and menstrual tracking data
caveats: Fitness trackers are not medical devices and would need FDA approval to alert to medical problems
Wrist-based heart rate and distance readings can be inaccurate during rapid arm motion or some exercise
Evidence that trackers improve health outcomes is limited
